subject: phase3_input_cost_containment
statement: Complete the Requests historical-control screen at its aggregate budget boundary and reject the current context-containment policy as sufficient for AgentTeam orchestration.
selected_option: retain the valid single result and cost-valid direct execution, stop before full mode, and require provider-free containment repair before any new SWE-EVO instance

alternatives.option: launch agentteam_full after the aggregate ceiling was crossed
alternatives.rejected_reason: The preregistered stop rule forbids another provider launch after cumulative usage exceeds 3000000 tokens.

alternatives.option: expand directly to a new SWE-EVO instance
alternatives.rejected_reason: Direct mode consumed 10.4196 times the treatment single-agent tokens, so the containment mechanism has not met its operational objective.

alternatives.option: discard direct-mode cost because its candidate patch conflicted with the evaluator patch
alternatives.rejected_reason: Patch conflict invalidates quality scoring but not provider-cost evidence; the execution completed and reported 100 percent usage coverage.

rationale: The final clean run reduced single-agent total tokens from 318079 to 266392, but increased direct-mode total tokens from 1093093 to 2775697. Direct mode issued 38 commands and received 538643 characters of command output, including one 332589-character pytest result. This demonstrates that the 4000-token model-context setting did not bound Codex CLI command output and did not prevent multi-step context replay. Cumulative usage reached 3042089 tokens, so the registered aggregate stop rule correctly prevented full mode from starting. The historical-control design and one repetition do not establish a general causal effect, but the direct-mode regression is sufficient to reject expansion under this policy.
expected_outcome: Preserve the bounded screen as negative cost-containment evidence and prevent further scored execution until command-output and multi-step context growth have enforceable provider-free controls.
